key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics, energy storage, and low-power neuromorphic computing must be co-designed so edge AI nodes can run reliably without centralized power-hungry data centers.
engineering_relevance: The paper highlights indoor photovoltaics and (anti)ferroelectrics as a practical materials pathway to power distributed intelligence at the edge with lower communication and compute energy costs.
method: Assess indoor photovoltaic requirements for distributed intelligence
Survey emerging materials for local energy harvesting and storage
Argue for (anti)ferroelectrics in electrostatic storage and in-memory neuromorphic devices
evidence_signal: This is a perspective article, so the support comes from requirements analysis and synthesis of emerging materials trends rather than new experimental data in the abstract.
watch_item: A key implementation challenge is that no single component is sufficient; edge systems will only work if harvesting, storage, and computing are integrated with adequate reliability and efficiency.
paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
